note: THE FIRST CLEAN ASTC CAPTURE ON THE PINNED DISTRICT, and the format A/B's other side against 2026-08-09-mobile-pinned-district-inventory.json (same district, same rect 5,-7,6,-6, same phone, rgba8 there and astc here). It is also the run that proved the fix in `requireFormatSupport`: the capture taken 3.5 h earlier on this same pak reported 20 of 20 world arrays refused with 'this texture is BC-compressed', cellsTotal 0 and a VOID warning — the upload gate computed its demand as `format !== RGBA8 ⇒ BC` while OSTEX_FORMAT_FEATURE already mapped ASTC4x4 to texture-compression-astc, so an ASTC pak passed the manifest gate and was then refused per array on a GPU that carries ASTC. That capture is NOT filed as a measurement (it measured an empty world); this one supersedes it. User-run on their own phone (Mali-G51, Android 10, 360x364 CSS px @ DPR 2), prebuilt app over localhost, pak build/phone-ls/pak buildTime 20:18 12-08-2026 (--textures astc --max-texture 256 --no-ao --bake-collision --map-objects-in-rect --platforms mobile; vehicles [admiral,infernus,comet], peds [bmycg,wmycr]). Its texture ceiling is filed as 2026-08-09-district-texture-budget-los-santos-centre.json, which predicted 25.4 MB resident for ASTC4x4 — the ledger reports 25.81, so the prediction holds.

device.note: No timestamp-query, so gpuPassMs/gpuPostMs/gpuProbeMs are ABSENT rather than zero. Mobile rows are never comparable to the desktop series.

world.note: Street level, the same working height as the 08-09 bytes row (25.7 m), so the byte columns are comparable to it. The 08-09 INVENTORY row was taken higher, so fps/frame numbers there are not a single-variable partner for these — residency is, because the texture format is the only thing that moves texture bytes.

runs.warnings: empty — the capture passes the collector's own validity test

bytes.note: 17 of 20 texture arrays read at this camera position, against 20 of 20 on the 08-09 bytes row from a wider view. NO cell-lod and NO collision requests — the collision finding of 201/1-01 reproduces on an ASTC pak.

frame.note: The histogram is not a vsync lock: 100 frames land in the 8-12 ms bins and 309 in the 30-38 ms band, so a world that can produce a 10 ms frame is not being held out of one.

residency.note: THE HEADLINE. Total 74.9 MB against 148 MB on the rgba8 side of this A/B — the texture category alone falls to 25.81 MB, a quarter of what the same texels cost as RGBA8, which is exactly what 200/2-02 was built for. And the second reading of the same table: `target` at 36.54 MB is now the LARGEST resident category, larger than every texture in the district. Render targets are a cost of RESOLUTION, not of content, and no amount of trimming the world touches them.

openQuestions: `cellsCreated` reads 2454 against 4 resident cells and 0 evictions. Either the counter counts something other than cells (draw groups?) or the streamer is re-creating. Nothing else in this capture looks like churn — blobMean 0.02 ms, uploadMean 0.18 — but the number cannot be cited until it is explained.

`target` 36.54 MB on a 360x364 CSS surface at DPR 2 (720x728 device px) is the largest single resident item. What the render-target chain allocates, and how much of it a map view needs, is unmeasured — and it is now the first place 201/1-03 should look, ahead of anything in the world.
One dt of 714.8 ms and one body of 154.1 ms (engine-frame 95.3 + overlay-2d 49.2). The window is 24 s, so a single stall of that size moves the mean; a longer window would say whether it recurs.

fps fell 33 -> 31 against the rgba8 row while memory halved. The camera height differs between the two (that row was taken higher), so this is NOT evidence that ASTC costs frame time — it is a reason the two rows may not be compared on fps at all.
